findings.title: upsampled_count SnQLFunction not marked private
findings.body: The newly added `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, unlike the surrounding private helpers (e.g. `thing_expression`, `count_at_least`). Without that flag the function becomes part of the user-exposed SnQL/Discover function surface, so end users could write `upsampled_count()` in their own queries. The function is only meaningful in conjunction with the project allowlist/sampling-rate pipeline, and emits `sum(sample_weight)` which has different semantics (and potential NULL-handling) from `count()`. Users invoking it directly outside of `organization_events_stats` will get counts that silently diverge from what they expect.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) silently drops NULL sample_weight rows
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` which is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. ClickHouse/SnQL `sum` ignores NULL arguments entirely, so any allowlisted-project event that has `sample_weight IS NULL` is silently omitted from the result, undercounting errors. The comment claims the schema guarantees `sample_weight` is non-null for allowlisted projects, but nothing in this helper (or in `discover.py`) enforces or even validates that invariant. There should be at minimum a guard that rejects the transformation (or coalesces `sample_weight` to a fallback) when the project list could contain NULL-weight events, otherwise dashboards/alerts that switch to upsampled counts will report numbers lower than the truth with no warning.

findings.title: transform only matches literal count(), misses aliased and surrounded variants
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` compares `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`. This single-equality test misses common variants that should still be upsampled: `count() as my_count`, `count() AS errors`, `count("id")` (counting a specific column), or `count()` surrounded by extra inner whitespace. As a result, a column written as `count() as count` (with explicit alias) will be passed through unchanged while the same column written as `count()` will be replaced with `upsampled_count() as count`, giving two clients querying the same metric different aggregations. The transform should at least recognise `count()` with a trailing `as <alias>` clause.

findings.title: _is_error_focused_query uses substring match on query string
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` decides based on `"event.type:error" in query`. The check is a raw substring match, so queries like `event.type:error_handled` (if such an alias is ever introduced) or any token that begins with `event.type:error` would be treated as error-focused and force the upsampled transformation on a dataset that may include non-error rows. A safer check parses the query tokens (e.g. via `event_search.parse_search_query`) and inspects the actual `event.type` value rather than doing a substring `in`.

findings.title: Error message wording regression adjacent to top_events validation
findings.body: The diff changes the response message from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. The new wording is grammatically cleaner, but it is bundled into a commit titled `feat(upsampling)` with no mention of an API/UX message change. Because this is a public 400 response body on `organization-events-stats`, any client that does an exact-string match on this `detail` value (e.g. localised tooling) will break. The change should either be split into its own commit or called out in the description.

findings.title: Unnecessary try/except around safe dict lookups
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps the chained `.get(...).get(...).get(...)` in a `try/except Exception: pass` and the `float(...)` conversion in another one. `dict.get` cannot raise for missing keys, and a malformed `client_sample_rate` string is the only realistic failure mode, which the second `try` already handles. The first try/except hides real bugs (e.g. `AttributeError` from a malformed contexts payload) and should be removed; only the `float()` conversion needs to be defensive.

findings.title: setUp reassigns self.user after login_as, breaking auth identity
findings.body: In `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, the test calls `self.login_as(user=self.user)` with the user that `APITestCase.setUp` created, then immediately overwrites `self.user = self.create_user()`. From that point on, `self.user` no longer refers to the authenticated user, and any tag, audit log entry, or future test that reads `self.user` will silently use the wrong identity. In particular the events stored right below use `self.user.email` / `self.user2.email` as the `sentry:user` tag, which means the test is asserting counts against events whose owner does not match the calling API user; if any later assertion (or downstream test) compares user identity this will fail.

findings.title: Stale upsampling eligibility cache has no invalidation hook
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the all-projects-in-allowlist result for 60 seconds, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided but never called from anywhere in the diff (no admin signal, option listener, or tests cover invalidation). If a project is added to or removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, requests for the next minute will continue to use the previous decision. In the worst case (allowlist shrinks while cache still says eligible) the endpoint will issue `sum(sample_weight)` queries for projects that no longer guarantee non-null `sample_weight`, potentially producing the silent undercount called out above. There should be an explicit invalidation call (or a much shorter TTL, or no cache) wired up before merging.

findings.title: Tests do not cover caching, invalidation, aliased count(), or NULL sample_weight
findings.body: The new test file covers the allowlist membership, the basic `count()` transform, the `event.type:error` substring check, and the dataset dispatch, but misses the most failure-prone paths: (1) `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is never tested, so the cache key construction (`hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`), cache-hit fast path, and 60s TTL behaviour are entirely uncovered; (2) `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` is never given aliased inputs (`count() as my_count`) so the limitation called out above is not pinned by a test; (3) there is no test asserting behaviour when a project in the allowlist emits events without `sample_weight`. Adding at least one cache-hit/miss test and an aliased-count test would prevent the cache and transform edge cases from regressing unnoticed.

findings.title: Cache key uses hash() of project_ids tuple
findings.body: The cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. While `hash(int)` is deterministic in CPython, mixing `hash()` of a derived structure into a cache key is fragile (it depends on tuple-hash internals and any future changes to them) and produces opaque keys that are hard to inspect/grep in Redis. A deterministic, explicit key like `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{','.join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))}"` (or a sha1 prefix) would be safer, debuggable, and immune to future interpreter changes.
